Using a single time point instead of the worst value in the period.
name: Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (original SOFA)

version.label: Original SOFA (Vincent et al. 1996), as tabulated in Sepsis-3 (Singer et al. 2016)
version.detail: Six organ systems scored 0–4, total 0–24. SOFA-2 (JAMA 2025) is a different version with new variables and thresholds and is not combined here.

purpose: Describes the degree of organ dysfunction in critically ill adults, repeatedly over time.

calculatorNotice.title: Original SOFA, not SOFA-2
calculatorNotice.message: Select the band for each organ using the worst value in the assessment period. Catecholamine doses are µg/kg/min given for at least 1 hour.

inputDefinitions.label: Cardiovascular
inputDefinitions.help: Doses in µg/kg/min, given for at least 1 hour.

inputDefinitions.label: Renal: creatinine, mg/dL (µmol/L), or urine output

calculationMethod.share: SOFA {total} (R{resp} C{coag} L{liver} CV{cv} CNS{cns} Re{renal})

resultStates.label: No organ dysfunction measured
resultStates.summary: No organ dysfunction measured by SOFA at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: SOFA covers six organ systems only; dysfunction elsewhere is not captured.

resultStates.label: SOFA {total}
resultStates.summary: Higher totals indicate more organ dysfunction. Change over time is often more informative than a single value.
resultStates.detail: Interpret each organ score and the trend with the clinical picture.

clinicalContext.text: Describes organ dysfunction across six systems, repeatedly during an ICU stay.
Sepsis-3 uses an acute change in total SOFA of 2 or more points as part of its sepsis criteria.

clinicalInsights.text: Record the timing and whether values are worst-in-24-hours; a pre-existing baseline (e.g. chronic kidney disease) affects interpretation.
The CNS component uses GCS, which is affected by sedation; many protocols use the best estimate of the unsedated GCS.

limitations.text: Published reproductions differ slightly at some boundaries (e.g. dopamine 5, creatinine 5.0); this implementation follows the Sepsis-3 table.
Values below 200 mmHg without respiratory support are not explicitly assigned in the table; follow local convention.

limitations: Catecholamine categories do not include vasopressin or newer agents.
Not designed as a mortality prediction tool for an individual patient.

confounders.effect: Lowers GCS independently of brain dysfunction.

guideSections.what: A score of dysfunction in six organ systems (respiratory, coagulation, liver, cardiovascular, CNS, renal), each 0–4.
guideSections.whenToUse: Serial description of organ dysfunction in the ICU; research and Sepsis-3 criteria.
guideSections.howToPerform: For each organ, select the band matching the worst value in the assessment period. The total is the sum of the six organ scores.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A descriptive and sequential measure; trends and organ-specific scores are interpreted with the clinical picture.
